title: Negroni
content: Equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth, stirred over ice, orange peel. Bitter, bracing, and impossible to improve. Three ingredients, no shaking, no citrus to juice - the easiest impressive cocktail in the book. Batch it in a bottle for parties.

title: Margarita
content: Two parts blanco tequila, one part lime, three-quarters part orange liqueur, shaken hard, salt rim optional but correct. Skip the sour mix forever. Bright, sour, crowd-pleasing - the default warm-weather party drink. Scale to pitchers by multiplying, not improvising.

title: Old Fashioned
content: Two ounces bourbon or rye, a sugar cube, two dashes Angostura, stirred with one big cube, orange peel. The cocktail that defines 'spirit-forward'. Five minutes, four ingredients, endless arguments about muddled fruit (don't). The whiskey drinker's starting point.

title: Daiquiri
content: White rum, fresh lime, simple syrup - shaken ice cold and strained into a coupe. Nothing like the frozen slush machine version: this is the bartender's handshake, the three-ingredient test of technique. Sour, clean, and gone in four sips.

title: Espresso Martini
content: Vodka, fresh espresso, coffee liqueur, a whisper of simple syrup, shaken violently for the foam crown. The revived modern classic and the most-requested drink at any party after 9pm. Pull the espresso just before shaking - stale coffee kills the foam.

title: Mojito
content: White rum, lime, sugar, mint gently pressed (not pulverized), topped with soda over crushed ice. Refreshing and low-effort once you stop over-muddling. The high-summer porch drink. Make crushed ice by whacking a towel-wrapped bag of cubes.

title: Manhattan
content: Two parts rye, one part sweet vermouth, two dashes Angostura, stirred silky and served up with a brandied cherry. The Old Fashioned's citified sibling - richer, rounder, more dangerous. Keep vermouth refrigerated after opening; dead vermouth is the #1 Manhattan crime.

title: Paloma
content: Tequila, fresh grapefruit, lime, pinch of salt, topped with soda (or grapefruit soda for the classic shortcut). Taller, lighter, and arguably better than a margarita on a hot day. The move for guests who say they don't like tequila.

title: Whiskey Sour with Egg White
content: Bourbon, lemon, simple syrup, egg white - dry-shaken first for foam, then shaken with ice. Silky, frothy, balanced; the egg white is flavorless but transforms the texture. Aquafaba substitutes perfectly for a vegan version. Garnish with bitters dashed through the foam.

title: French 75
content: Gin, lemon, simple syrup, shaken, topped with champagne in a flute. Celebration in a glass - brunch, weddings, New Year's. Prosecco or cava work fine; nobody at the party can tell. Batch the gin-lemon-syrup base ahead and top to order.

title: Mai Tai
content: Aged rum, lime, orange curaçao, orgeat (almond syrup), rum float - the real 1944 Trader Vic's recipe, not the pineapple-juice imposter. Nutty, complex, and strong. The gateway to tiki; orgeat is the one specialty bottle worth buying.

title: Aperol Spritz
content: Three parts prosecco, two parts Aperol, one part soda, built over ice in a wine glass with an orange slice. The lowest-effort cocktail in this collection and the lowest ABV - the daytime drink. Assembles in 60 seconds for however many guests just arrived.

title: Gimlet
content: Gin and lime cordial - modern versions use fresh lime plus simple syrup, shaken. Cleaner and drier than a daiquiri, sharper than a martini. Two and a half ounces of gin means it drinks stronger than it tastes; pace accordingly.

title: Penicillin
content: Blended scotch, lemon, honey-ginger syrup, with a peated Islay scotch float on top. The most famous cocktail invented this century: smoky, spicy, and soothing at once. The honey-ginger syrup takes 15 minutes to make and elevates everything else it touches too.

title: Dark 'n' Stormy
content: Dark rum floated over ginger beer with a squeeze of lime, built in a highball. Two ingredients plus lime, zero technique, maximum reward - the sailing drink. Use a fiery ginger beer; sweet ones make it flabby.

title: Martini
content: Gin (or vodka), dry vermouth to taste - start 4:1 - stirred glacially cold, lemon twist or olive. The most personal drink in the canon: ratio, garnish, and temperature are identity statements. Freeze the glass; a warm martini is a ruined martini.

title: Virgin Mule (Non-Alcoholic)
content: Fiery ginger beer, fresh lime, a few dashes of non-alcoholic bitters, mint, over crushed ice in a copper mug. The best zero-proof option that doesn't feel like a consolation prize. Add muddled cucumber for a garden version.

title: Sazerac
content: Rye whiskey, sugar, Peychaud's bitters, in a chilled glass rinsed with absinthe, lemon peel expressed and discarded. New Orleans' official cocktail and a ritual as much as a drink. The absinthe rinse perfumes everything - do not skip it, do not overdo it.
